answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A jade delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A inlet check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A nectar penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 6788 identities need 6788 bonds of 80 tokens, 46116 dollars of hardware and 19 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
